title: Lockheed Martin sets its third quarter report for Thursday
summary: Lockheed Martin announced that it will release third quarter earnings before the stock market opens on October 22, followed by a call with investors at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. The stock closed Tuesday at $548.71.
why: Every three months a company reports how much it sold and earned. If the numbers or the outlook differ from what analysts expected, the stock can jump or drop quickly, so report days are often the bumpiest.

title: GE Aerospace reports strong quarter, raises outlook
summary: GE Aerospace shared third quarter results on October 20. Orders grew 49% to $19.0 billion, adjusted revenue rose 18% to $13.3 billion, and adjusted earnings per share reached $2.25. The company said it is raising its 2026 guidance across the board.
why: A company's guidance is its own forecast for the year. Raising it is usually good news. But the stock still fell 3.7% in our data, which shows that prices depend on what investors hoped for, not only on the results.

title: Fed chair's speech makes a rate hike this month less likely
summary: Speaking at the IMF meetings in Bangkok, the Fed chair gave no clear signal about future rate moves. Afterward, traders cut the odds of a hike at the October 27 and 28 meeting to under 15%, down from about 27%.
why: The Fed sets short term interest rates. Higher rates make borrowing cost more and can slow company profits, so stocks often wobble when traders expect a hike. The meeting is the next big date to watch.

title: 10 year Treasury yield stays near 5.1%
summary: The yield on the 10 year US Treasury note ended last week near 5.12%. That is a bit lower than earlier in October, when it hit its highest level since 2002.
why: A Treasury is a loan to the US government, and the yield is the interest it pays. When safe bonds pay more, stocks have to look more attractive to compete, so high yields can pull stock prices down.
